newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz to introduce cheaper motor tariff.
newsitem.headline: Allianz to introduce cheaper motor tariff.

text.p: German insurance group Allianz AG said on Thursday it would next year run a trial with a second, cheaper tariff in motor insurance which will be offered parallel to the normal tariff.
An Allianz spokesman said in response to an inquiry that the group would introduce the new model in April in three "testbeds", the cities of Munich, Berlin and Hamburg.

Allianz agents will then offer two parallel motor tariffs. The normal tariff will be slightly improved as far as benefits are concerned, for example by introducing an improved system of keeping a no claims bonus following a claim.
Alongside this a second tariff will be on offer, which is some 10 percent cheaper.

The benefits under the cheaper tariff will be slightly reduced, for example a 1,000 mark excess for an accident involving wild animals, a 20 percent excess for theft in eastern European countries, and a stronger drop in the no claims bonus after a claim.
"A number of different variations will be tested," said Heilmann.

Allianz' market share in motor insurance business is stagnating at 16 percent, while rival low-cost insurers, for example HUK-Coburg, have been able to expand their shares considerably in the last years.
With its cheaper tariff, Germany's largest motor insurer aims to put its salesforce in a position to keep pace with the competition.
However, the agents receive less commission for completing contracts under the cheaper tariff, a source of contention within the Allianz salesforce.
